clusters.name: Your grandfather Clifford's return, 1989–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Clifford's return into the family in early 1989, within three years: your late nights began that autumn, you moved into the rebuilt Hollin Road house with your mother and Desmond and his children, you let your mother fill in your college forms, your wrist injury stopped your playing in your first term at the conservatory, Rafe moved out after a blow-up between you, and you found yourself lost and low unable to get going with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry. These shifts are yours, piling up from your late teens into early adulthood around your grandfather's reappearance and your move into a crowded household.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer, 2001–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred being found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within two years: you ran out of steam for performing, you had a disastrous audition and were done with performing, you grew distant from family and friends, you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, you met Marisol and moved to Fenwick, you split from her within the year and sank into a deep depression, you could not face your family and relied on friends instead. Your shifts cluster around the same time as your grandmother's diagnosis and the end of your performing life, both falling in 2001 and 2002.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within two and a half years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, and in October 2019 a wave of events hit in quick succession—Wren swamped with one thing after another, you overfunctioning to settle her, her family fused in constant contact, then at her family's lake house for her mother's retirement you woke from early hours unable to sleep and could only pull back, and Wren anxious when you had no sleep at family occasions. These shifts are yours and Wren's together, with her family's fusion backdrop, showing you struggling to find your footing in the wider family system you joined.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
